title: Capacity and Transmission Charge Bases - Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts
content:
For Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts, the method of computing a pass-through capacity charge and a pass-through transmission charge is the same on every Beacon Ridge C&I structure, and no structure trues up past charges when the grid operator revises a tag.

## Bases by structure

| Structure | Capacity charge basis | Transmission charge basis | Retroactive true-up on a tag revision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beacon Ridge C&I Real-Time Index | PLC kW times capacity price (USD per MW-day) times days, divided by 1000 | NSPL kW times transmission rate (USD per MW-day) times days, divided by 1000 | no |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Block and Index | same | same | no |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed Energy with Capacity and Transmission Pass-Through | same | same | no |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed Energy with Capacity Pass-Through | same | same | no |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed All-In | same | same | no |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed All-In Renewable | same | same | no |

PLC kW is the facility's peak load contribution (its capacity tag). NSPL kW is its network service peak load (its transmission tag). The days are the billing days of the cycle.

## Stated in words

- A pass-through capacity charge is the capacity tag in kW multiplied by the capacity price in US dollars per MW-day, multiplied by the billing days, and divided by 1000.
- A pass-through transmission charge is the transmission tag in kW multiplied by the transmission rate in US dollars per MW-day, multiplied by the billing days, and divided by 1000.
- When the grid operator revises a tag, charges already billed are not trued up retroactively on any structure.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical inputs)

A capacity tag of 1850.0 kW, a capacity price of 269.92 USD per MW-day and a 31-day cycle give 1850.0 multiplied by 269.92 multiplied by 31, divided by 1000, which is 15479.912, shown on the bill as $15479.91 after rounding to the cent.
